stem: To diagnose the medical conditions, MRi technique is used. Which is not used in MRi?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a medical imaging technique. To obtain images of body organs through MRI, a strong magnetic field and radio waves are used. It is also called Magnetic Resonance Tomography (MRT). Both X-rays and gamma rays are high-frequency ionizing radiation, meaning they have sufficient energy to remove electrons from an atom or molecule. In both ultrasound and MRI, no ionizing radiation is used.

stem: The process of determining the relative positions of genes on a chromosome is called -

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The process of finding the relative positions of genes on a chromosome is called gene mapping. It is used to determine gene order and to calculate the distance between genes.

stem: What is the expanded form of the term ‘mRNA’ that has been widely discussed since the beginning of the pandemic?
expl: The expanded form of mRNA is Messenger Ribonucleic acid. Messenger RNA is a type of single-stranded RNA that is involved in protein synthesis. mRNA-based vaccines were developed to prevent COVID-19.

stem: Which one of the following can be used for biological control of mosquitoes?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Gambusia fish can be used for the biological control of mosquitoes. Gambusia species, popularly known as mosquito fish, are used in many countries as a bio-control measure to check the transmission of vector-borne diseases.

stem: Angora wool is extracted from :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Angora wool is obtained from the Angora rabbit. Mohair is obtained from the Angora goat.

stem: A nail is nailed into the trunk of a tree at a point 1 m from the soil level. After 2 years the nail will :
expl: If a nail is hammered into the trunk of a tree at a height of 1 m above the soil surface, then after two years it will remain at the same place. This is because the length of a plant increases due to the apical meristem. The apical meristem is present at the tips of the root and shoot. Since the nail is fixed in the stem, the permanent tissue does not divide in this condition.

stem: The Nobel Prize for developing treatment of Parkinson’s disease was given to:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: For the development of treatment for Parkinson’s disease, the Swedish neuroscientist Arvid Carlsson was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in the year 2000. He discovered that dopamine is an important neurotransmitter in the brain, and in Parkinson’s disease the nerve cells that produce dopamine in the basal ganglia gradually degenerate, which leads to tremor, rigidity, and akinesia. His research showed that Parkinson’s disease occurs due to a deficiency of dopamine in certain parts of the brain, and an effective medicine (L-dopa) can be developed for it.

stem: ‘AVAHAN’ the indian segment of the ‘Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation’, is engaged in the prevention of-

stem: The laughing gas used by doctors as an anaesthesia is -
expl: The gas used by doctors as an anaesthetic is nitrous oxide. It is a colourless, odourless gas.

stem: When antigens are introduced in to the body through vaccination antibodies are produced to fight off infection

options.label: a
options.text: By both B and T cells

expl: When an antigen enters the body through a vaccine, antibodies are produced by B lymphocytes (a special type of white blood cell) to fight infection. When an antigen comes in contact with B cells, it causes the B cell to divide and form clones. These cloned B cells release millions of antibodies into the blood circulation and the lymphatic system. Antibodies strengthen the body’s immune system.

stem: At what age can polio drops be given?
expl: Generally, polio drops are given to a newborn at birth, which provide initial protection to the baby. The first dose of the polio injection is given six weeks after birth.

stem: A substance added to food containing fats and oils is called
expl: The substance added to fat- and oil-containing food is called an antioxidant (anti-oxidizing agent). Antioxidants are chemicals that stop or slow down the process of oxidation.

stem: Tomato is a natural source of which acid?
expl: Tomato is a natural source of oxalic acid. Its chemical formula is (COOH). Oxalic acid is an organic compound that is also found in small amounts in green leafy vegetables, such as spinach. Acetic acid is found in vinegar. Citric acid is found in citrus fruits.

stem: Insectivorous plants grow in the soil deficient in -

expl: Insectivorous plants grow in soil where nitrogen is deficient. They fulfill their nitrogen requirement by feeding on insects.

stem: What are salt-loving plants called?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Halophytes are salt-loving plants that grow in saline soils and coastal regions. They survive by removing or storing excess salt, having succulent leaves, and reducing water loss. They maintain osmotic balance using solutes like proline and sugar. Examples include mangroves (Avicennia, Rhizophora), Salicornia and Atriplex.

stem: Who discovered bacteria?
expl: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek is known as the father of microbiology. In 1676, he identified bacteria using a single-lens microscope he made himself.

stem: The ones who discovered photoperiodism in plants are -

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Photoperiodism in plants was discovered by Garner and Allard. The response of plants to the duration and timing of light is called “photoperiodism.”
